story_text.value:
Hey HN , I made Plot because I kept losing track of my own projects.

It's easy nowadays to have 10 vibe-coded projects running simultaneously, but once you have so many projects going on, it's very hard to stay on top of them. You reply to a question Claude asked about Project A, open Project B to debug a little bit, shifting to Project C, build a marketing page, and when you go back to Project A, you've already forget where you left off, what you were going to do next, or why you decided to use that library.

I made Plot to help with that. It’s a Chrome extension that opens in your new tab, so you can't miss it. Here’s what you can do with it:

- In the 2D view, you can resize each project’s plot. Make the ones you want to focus on bigger, and the others smaller.

- In the 3D view, each project is a building. The more tasks you finish and the more decisions and learnings you record, the taller it grows. You can see where you’ve been putting your effort.

- Click into a project to manage its backlog and to-dos, keep a record of what you’ve shipped, and write down decisions and learnings. Markdown is supported.

- In Stats, you can see your recent activity across projects. You can also click a date on the calendar to look back at what you were doing that day.

- There’s no AI feature in it. Everything is stored locally in your browser. I wanted something lightweight and easy to use that helps me keep track of what I’m building, and looks pretty cool while doing it.

title.value: Show HN: Plot, a 3D project tracker in your Chrome new tab

story_text.value:
Hey HN! Recently Meta wrapped up their Global Developer Hackathon (https://dev.meta.ai/events/global-hackathon) which had a $1M prize pool (!!): 34K developers applied, 20K accepted, and over 5K projects were submitted.

With this crazy volume, it was infeasible to rank or even shortlist the best projects with human review. On the other hand, AI scoring against a rubric led to disappointing results.

In an effort to surface and spotlight the best projects, I built MetaArena (https://meta-hackathon.com/). It compares just two projects head-to-head, let's you pick which you thought was the stronger project, and places them on a leaderboard using the same algo platforms like LLMArena and DesignArena use to rank AI models (Bradley-Terry).

Check it out, at the very least I hope you find a cool project or two here that inspire you. Lmk if you have any feedback on the arena/leaderboard!

story_text.value:
When TripCase shut down, I couldn't find an Android or web replacement I actually liked using. Especially with live flight tracking for gate and delay notifications.

So I built TripCoral. Airports and aviation authorities actually give out a lot of FIDS and air-traffic data for free: Avinor (Norway), Swedavia (Sweden), Schiphol (Netherlands), FAA SWIM (United States) etc. Instead of paying a commercial data broker, I wrote a Go collector that pulls from 100s of feeds covering ~1900 airports.

Forward your confirmation emails (flights, hotels, cars, dinner bookings) or enter a flight number, and it puts the whole trip on one timeline, works offline, and follows travel day live: check-in desks, gates, delays, security queues, indoor gate-to-gate walk times on tight connections, and baggage belts where published.

Google Play: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.tripcoral....

Web app: https://app.tripcoral.com

If you have a flight coming up, I'd love feedback on the UX or anything to make it more useful for travelers!

title.value: Show HN: TripCoral – Free itinerary and live updates from public flight data

story_text.value:
Hi HN. Builderoom is a site where indie devs, designers and makers list what they build, and you can look for stuff by just describing what you need, like "physics simulation running in the browser". Browsing and normal keyword search work without an account.

Why I made it: a lot of the time I know what I need but not what the thing is called, so keyword search doesn't help much. And whenever I ship something, every launch site wants the same long form again.
